propositions: The completion-verification close gate enters infinite tool-call loops during the verify step, exhausting the step budget and surfacing a bare LLMError with null diagnostic instead of a verdict.
The current tool_step_limit empty-filter rewrite in agent_call.py causes Bedrock/Anthropic 400 errors because toolConfig becomes undefined after tool calls have occurred in the history.

Runaway cycles are distinguishable from healthy breadth via a windowed distinct-ratio metric (window 24, threshold ≤0.50) computed in usage_log, but this signal is not currently used to detect and abort loops during execution.

The repetition diagnostic and usage counters must be recorded durably and surfaced in the gate_error_v1 sidecar so operators can distinguish loop-caused budget exhaustion from genuine out-of-room scenarios.

Recovery after a tool-call runaway must be reachable by extending exception handling in CompletionAgentStep.run and routing detected runaways through bounded recovery with fresh per-criterion evidence.
